finalText:
**Two things are usually behind this.**

React does not skip a child when the parent renders. By default every child re-renders, same props or not. `React.memo` is what turns that off.

Once the child is wrapped in `React.memo`, props get compared one by one with `Object.is`. An object, array, or function written inside the parent is a brand new value each render. So the comparison fails even though the contents look identical.

The fix:
1. Wrap the child in `React.memo`.
2. Wrap object and array props in `useMemo`.
3. Wrap function props in `useCallback`.

A re-render on its own is not a bug. Only chase it if you can measure it being slow.
